title: Conspiracy and the substantive offense — no merger; Wharton's Rule scope
signal: Two or more persons agree to commit a substantive crime and succeed; the call is whether they can be convicted of both.
student_move: Check Wharton's Rule first. If the substantive crime is one that by definition requires two persons (bigamy, adultery, incest, dueling), conspiracy merges and only the substantive stands. Otherwise, both stack.
tiny_rule: Conspiracy and the substantive offense are separate crimes; arson is not a Wharton's Rule crime.
trap: The merger myth is the dominant trap. Many students half-remember that 'conspiracy merges' and walk into the but-not-both answer.

title: Breaking element — constructive breaking by fraud
signal: Entry obtained by a false-pretenses pretext (utility worker, repair person, fellow church member) at night, with intent to commit a felony at the moment of entry.
student_move: Cut physical-damage and voluntary-opening rationales with the Gold Key; cut intent-after-entry with the timing rule.
tiny_rule: Constructive breaking includes fraud-induced entry; consent procured by fraud is not effective consent.
trap: The everyday conception of 'breaking' fuses it with physical force; the common-law rule is broader.

title: Asportation minimum vs. removal / sale
signal: Customer slips a small item from an open display, takes a few steps, and is stopped before leaving the building.
student_move: Cut 'must leave the building' and 'stopped before she sold' on visible defects; the slight-movement answer is residual.
tiny_rule: Asportation is satisfied by even minimal movement; the property need not leave the building and sale is not an element.
trap: Conflating asportation with a successful shoplifting exit, or looking for a sale element that does not exist.

title: Forgery - false making is the actus reus
signal: A finder of unused checks fills in a check, signs the owner's name without authority, and plans to cash it. The owner has not actually lost money, and the check has not been cashed.
student_move: Cut tiered-absolute overclaims (checks have apparent legal efficacy) and wrong-element traps (uttering is not the actus reus of forgery). Then apply the Gold Key: the victim's actual loss is not an element of forgery; the false making is the actus reus.
tiny_rule: Forgery is complete at the false making of a writing with apparent legal efficacy and intent to defraud; loss and successful uttering are not elements.
trap: The lay intuition 'no harm, no foul' is wrong. The victim need not actually lose money, and the forger need not successfully utter the document.

title: Receiving stolen property — receipt-time knowledge is the dispositive element
signal: Buyer purchases property at a normal price from a trusted seller; nothing suggests the property is stolen; the buyer learns the truth later; the buyer promptly returns the property. The call is whether the buyer is guilty of receiving stolen property.
student_move: Test whether the defendant had knowledge or belief that the property was stolen at the moment of receipt. If not, the offense fails on the mens rea element and the rest of the analysis is unnecessary. Later knowledge does not retroactively supply the missing mens rea. The fact that the property was stolen before the defendant received it is necessary but not sufficient.
tiny_rule: Receiving stolen property requires that the defendant know or believe the property was stolen at the time she received control of it; later knowledge does not retroactively supply the receipt-time mens rea.
trap: The stolen-before-purchase trap is the dominant misconception. Many students reason that because the property was stolen, anyone who received it must be guilty. The error is that the offense also requires knowledge or belief at the time of receipt — a good-faith purchaser is not guilty.

title: Embezzlement vs larceny vs false pretenses
signal: owner entrusts property to a repair/restoration shop, shop lawfully accepts, shop then sells to a third party and keeps the proceeds
student_move: Cut the colloquial-larceny overclaim (A) and the consent-coverage overclaim (B) and the false-pretenses misfit (D); the residual is embezzlement (C).
tiny_rule: Lawful possession at the outset re-routes the offense from larceny to embezzlement.
trap: Everyday English treats 'theft' as a synonym for larceny, but the theft-offense distinction turns on the manner in which the defendant first came into possession.

title: Larceny — temporary-use and return is not larceny
signal: Taking of another's personal property without permission, defined short-term use, actual return plan, police stop before return
student_move: Lock the intent-to-permanently-deprive element on the temporary-use-and-return fact pattern. Cut C (any unauthorized use) on the universal-quantifier marker. Cut D (asportation) on the missing-intent element. Cut B (power tools not personal property) on the obvious-chattel counterexample.
tiny_rule: Larceny requires the intent to permanently deprive; short, safe, return-planned borrowing is not larceny.
trap: The 'any unauthorized use' shortcut that fuses trespass with the common-law definition.

title: Wharton Count Check
signal: Wharton’s Rule plus extra people in the agreement
student_move: Count required participants first; count actual agreement participants second.
trap: Stopping at the two-party offense and missing the extra-party exception.

title: Custody is not possession
student_move: Ask whether the worker had custody only, lawful possession, title by deception, or no taking.

title: Miranda Fruit Is Not Fourth-Amendment Fruit
signal: Unwarned but voluntary statement leads police to a physical object.
student_move: Pin the offered evidence: statement or object.
tiny_rule: Statement out; voluntary-statement physical fruit generally in.
trap: Importing all-fruits suppression from Fourth Amendment doctrine.

title: Warnings are not a pressure shield
signal: Stem gives Miranda warnings and then coercive pressure facts.
student_move: Separate warning/form facts from voluntariness facts.
tiny_rule: Coercion can defeat admissibility even after warnings.
trap: Picking the warning answer because it sounds procedurally clean.

title: Bad arrest is not automatic dismissal
signal: Unlawful arrest + motion to dismiss + independent evidence
student_move: Separate the violation from the requested remedy.
tiny_rule: Suppress tainted evidence when applicable; do not dismiss charges supported by independent evidence.
trap: Treating illegality as automatic case erasure.

title: Plain feel: immediate apparentness, not tactile investigation
signal: Lawful frisk; nonweapon object; officer keeps feeling it to identify it.
student_move: Stop the frisk at the moment the officer knows the item is not a weapon unless contraband is already immediately apparent.
tiny_rule: Manipulation to identify contraband breaks plain feel.
trap: Treating Terry frisk as permission to search for drugs.

title: Duress requires now-pressure.
signal: Future threat, remote threatener, time to seek help.
student_move: Cut fear-only and family-only answers; keep the answer that checks imminence.
tiny_rule: Duress is immediate-threat plus no reasonable escape, not fear alone.
trap: Sympathy for a believable family threat.

title: Same offense, new label
signal: Police say they only want to ask about a smaller version of the charged incident.
student_move: Do not stop at the label. Compare the factual event and offense substance.
tiny_rule: Post-charge Sixth Amendment protection follows the same offense in substance.
trap: The label-only answer sounds precise but is too shallow.

title: Fact mistake / law mistake split
signal: One actor misunderstands ownership facts; another understands facts but misunderstands legality.
student_move: First label each mistake as fact or law, then apply the specific-intent Gold Key.
tiny_rule: Specific-intent fact mistake can negate intent; law mistake generally cannot.
trap: Treating all sincere mistakes the same or requiring reasonableness for every mistake.

title: Insanity tests: cognition vs volition
signal: Stem gives M'Naghten plus irresistible impulse.
student_move: Match facts to lanes before picking.
trap: Treating one lane as the whole insanity defense.

title: Misdemeanor label is not a death cause
signal: A misdemeanor is followed by a death from a separate event.
student_move: Ask whether the misdemeanor produced the death, not merely whether it came first.
tiny_rule: No cause link, no misdemeanor manslaughter.

title: Person warrant vs place warrant
signal: Arrest warrant for suspect + suspect inside someone else's home.
student_move: Ask whose home is being entered.
tiny_rule: Own home may be Payton; third-party home needs Steagald search warrant or exception.
